    #CA1

    #Question 1

    Fluid velocity at inlet,

    m˙=ρA1​V1​

    V1​=1000(0.0113)14​

    V1​=1.2389 m/s

    Fluid velocity at outlet,

    m˙=ρA2​V2​

    V2​=1000(0.0007)14​

    V2​=20 m/s

    Pressure at inlet,

    P1​+21​ρV1​2+z1​=P2​+21​ρV2​2+z2​

    P1​=21​ρ(V2​2−V1​2)+(z2​−z1​)

    P1​=21​(1000)(202−1.23892)+0.3

    P1​=199.23 kPa

    Linear momentum along x-axis,

    ∑Fx​=(m˙V)out​−(m˙V)in​

    FH​+P1​A1​+P2​A2​=m˙(V2​−V1​)

    FH​+(199.23×103)(0.0113)=14(−20−1.2389)

    FH​=−2548.7 N

    Horizontal force acts to the left.

    Linear momentum along y-axis,

    ∑Fy​=(m˙V)out​−(m˙V)in​

    FV​=0

    Fluid has no velocity along the y-axis.
    Thus, there is no vertical force.

    #Question 2

    Fluid velocity at inlet,

    Q=A1​V1​

    V1​=π(0.15)20.6​

    V1​=8.4883 m/s

    Fluid velocity at outlet,

    Q=A2​V2​

    V2​=π(0.125)20.6​

    V2​=12.223 m/s

    Applying the energy equation,

    W˙in​+m˙(ρP1​​+21​V1​2+gz1​)=W˙out​+m˙(ρP2​​+21​V2​2+gz2​)

    ρQ(ρP1​​+21​V1​2)=W˙tur​+ρQ(ρP2​​+21​V2​2)

    W˙tur​=ρQ[ρP1​−P2​​+21​(V1​2−V2​2)]

    W˙tur​=1000(0.6)[1000(1.2/0.76)(100×103)​+21​(8.48832−12.2232)]

    W˙tur​=71531.7 W

    Electric power output,

    η=Ptur​Pelec​​

    0.6=71531.7Pelec​​

    Pelec​=42919.0 W

    #Question 3

    #Part (a)

    Fluid velocity at outlet,

    Q=A1​V1​=A2​V2​

    0.05(2)=0.02V2​

    V2​=5 m/s

    Using Bernoulli’s equation,

    P1​+21​ρV1​2+ρgz1​=P2​+21​ρV2​2+ρgz2​

    P1​+21​(1000)(22)+1000(9.81)(0.4)=21​(1000)(52)

    P1​=6576 Pa (gauge pressure)

    #Part (b)

    Linear momentum along x-axis,

    ∑Fx​=(m˙V)out​−(m˙V)in​

    Fx​=ρA1​V1​(−V2​cos30°−0)

    Fx​=ρA1​V1​(−V2​cos30°)

    Fx​=1000(0.05)(2)(−5cos30°)

    Fx​=−433.01 N

    Horizontal force acts to the left.

    Linear momentum along y-axis,

    ∑Fy​=(m˙V)out​−(m˙V)in​

    Fy​−P1​A1​−mg=m˙[−V2​sin30°−(−V1​)]

    Fy​−P1​A1​−ρVg=ρA1​V1​(−V2​sin30°+V1​)

    Fy​−6576(0.05)−1000(0.01)(9.81)=1000(0.05)(2)(−5sin30°+2)

    Fy​=376.9 N

    Vertical force acts upwards.

    #Part (c)

    Horizontal motion of the nozzle does not affect the answers.

    • Momentum equation uses fluid velocity relative to the CV
    • Since fluid is enclosed within the control volume, inlet and

    #Question 4

    #Part (a)

    Using Bernoulli’s equation,

    ρgPnoz​​+2gVnoz​2​+znoz​=ρgP0​​+2gV0​2​+z0​

    2(9.81)42​=2(9.81)V0​2​+0.2

    V0​=3.4751 m/s

    Mass flow rate of fluid,

    m˙tot​=ρAnoz​Vnoz​

    m˙tot​=1000(0.001)(4)

    m˙tot​=4 kg/s

    Linear momentum along z-axis,

    ∑Fz​=(m˙V)out​−(m˙V)in​

    FV​=m˙tot​(0−V0​)

    FV​=−13.9 N

    Vertical force acts downwards.

    #Part (b)

    Using Bernoulli’s equation,

    V0​=V1​=V2​=3.4751 m/s

    Mass flow rate through Outlet 1,

    m˙1​=ρA1​V1​

    m˙1​=1000(0.0004)(3.4751)

    m˙1​=1.39 kg/s

    Mass flow rate through Outlet 2,

    m˙2​=m˙tot​−m˙1​

    m˙2​=4−1.39

    m˙2​=2.61 kg/s

    Exit area of Outlet 2,

    m˙2​=ρA2​V2​

    A2​=1000(3.4751)2.61​

    A2​=0.00075106 m2=7.5106 cm2

    #Part (c)

    Tangential velocity of outlets,

    Vt​=rω=0.2(5)=1 m/s

    Fluid velocity at Outlet 1 relative to CV,

    V1,abs​=V1​cos30°+Vt​

    V1,abs​=3.4751cos30°+1

    V1,abs​=4.01 m/s

    Fluid velocity at Outlet 2 relative to CV,

    V2,abs​=−V2​+Vt​

    V2,abs​=−3.4751+1

    V2,abs​=−2.4751 m/s

    Velocity of the fluid at the outlet is negative
    as it points in the opposite direction of spin.

    Assume resisting torque acts in the anticlockwise direction.

    Angular momentum about z-axis,

    ∑Tz​=m˙(r×V)out​−m˙(r×V)in​

    Tz​=m˙1​(rV1.abs​)+m˙2​(rV2,abs​)

    Tz​=1.39(0.2)(4.01)+2.61(0.2)(−2.4751)

    Tz​=−0.17722 Nm

    Since computed value is negative, resisting torque acts in the clockwise direction.

    #Question 5

    #Part (a)

    For the inlet, draw a streamline from a point far from the inlet.

    ρgP0​​+2gV0​2​+z0​=ρgP1​​+2gV1​2​+z1​

    0+0+0=ρgP1​​+2gV1​2​+0

    P1​=−21​ρV1​2

    For the outlet, the streamlines of the outflow are straight. Thus, the
    pressure difference across streamlines is the atmospheric pressure.

    P2​=0

    #Part (b)

    #Part (i)

    Linear momentum along x-axis,

    ∑Fx​=(m˙V)out​−(m˙V)in​

    Fx​−P1​A1​=m˙[−V2​cos60°−(−V1​)]

    Fx​−(−21​ρV1​2)A1​=ρA1​V1​(−V2​cos60°+V1​)

    Fx​=ρAV2(−cos60°+1)−21​ρAV2

    Fx​=ρAV2(0.5−cos60°)

    Linear momentum along y-axis,

    ∑Fy​=(m˙V)out​−(m˙V)in​

    Fy​=m˙(V2​sin60°−0)

    Fy​=ρAV2sin60°

    Using Pythagoras theorem,

    Fsup​=Fx​2+Fy​2​

    Fsup​2=[ρAV2(0.5−cos60°)]2+[ρAV2sin60°]2

    Fsup​2=(ρA)2V4[(0.5−cos60°)2+(sin60°)2]

    0.052=(1.232)(0.012)[(0.5−cos60°)2+(sin60°)2]V4

    V=2.1665 m/s

    #Part (ii)

    Using the energy equation,

    hin​+ρgP1​​+2gV2​+z1​=hout​+ρgP2​​+2gV2​+z2​

    hcomp​+ρgP1​​+0+z1​=2g1.5V2​+0+0+0

    hcomp​−2gV2​+z1​=2g1.5V2​

    hcomp​=2g2.5V2​−z1​

    hcomp​=2(9.81)2.5(2.1665)2​−0.1

    hcomp​=0.49810 m

    Power input to compressor,

    W˙comp​=m˙ghcomp​

    W˙comp​=1.23(0.01)(2.1665)(9.81)(0.49810)

    W˙comp​=0.13021 W

    #Part (iii)

    Assume resisting torque acts in the anticlockwise direction.

    Note that the pressure at the inlet contributes to the torque.

    Angular momentum about rigid support,

    ∑T=m˙(r×V)out​−m˙(r×V)in​

    T+P1​A1​h=m˙[L2​(−V2​sin60°)−h(V1​)]

    T−21​(1.23)(2.1665)2(0.01)(0.1)=1.23(0.01)(2.1665)[0.8(−2.1665sin60°)−0.1(2.1665)]

    T=−0.042885 Nm

    Since computed value is negative, resisting torque acts in the clockwise direction.

    #Question 6

    Absolute velocity of water relative to CV,

    Vabs​=−W2​cosθ+VCV​

    Vabs​=−W2​cos30°+r2​ω

    Vabs​=−1cos30°+0.1(30)

    Vabs​=2.1340 m/s

    Note that W2​ is negative as it points in the opposite direction of spin.

    T=m˙r2​Vabs​

    T=15.708(0.1)(2.1340)

    T=3.3520 Nm

    Since computed value is positive, assumed direction for torque is correct.

    Power required to operate pump,

    W˙pump​=Tω

    W˙pump​=3.3520(30)

    W˙pump​=100.56 W

    #CA2

    #Question 1

    Volume flow rate function,

    Q=f(μ, LΔP​, b)

    Expressing the variables in terms of reference dimensions:

    • Q=sm3​=TL3​=L3T−1
    • μ=m⋅skg​=LTM​=ML−1T−1
    • LΔP​=m3⋅s2kg⋅m​=L2T2M​=ML−2T−2
    • b=m=L

    Number of Π-groups,

    k=4−3=1

    Equation for Π-group,

    Π1​=(μa⋅LΔP​b⋅bc)Q

    Comparing coefficients,

    M0L0T0=(ML−1T−1)a(ML−2T−2)b(L)c(L3T−1)

    0=a+b

    0=−a−2b+c+3

    0=−a−2b−1

    ∴ a=1     b=−1     c=−4

    Volume flow rate function,

    Π1​=ΔP⋅b4μL​Q

    If b is doubled,

    Π=ΔP(2b)4μL​Q=ΔP(16b4)μL​Q

    The volume flow rate will decrease by a factor of 16.

    #Question 2

    #Part (a)

    Torque function,

    T=f(R2​, ω, n, ρ, d, θ, Q)

    From the given Π-term, repeating variables are R2​, ρ, and Q.

    Note that torque is the variable we are interested in finding,
    thus the other three variables must be repeating variables.

    Number of Π-groups required,

    k=8−3=5

    Equations for each Π-group,

    Π1​=(R2​a1​⋅ρb1​⋅Qc1​)ω

    Π2​=(R2​a2​⋅ρb2​⋅Qc2​)n

    Π3​=(R2​a3​⋅ρb3​⋅Qc3​)d

    Π4​=(R2​a4​⋅ρb4​⋅Qc4​)θ

    Π5​=ρQ2TR2​​

    Comparing coefficients for Π1​,

    M0L0T0=(L)a1​(ML−3)b1​(L3T−1)c1​(T−1)

    ∴ a1​=3     b1​=0     c1​=−1

    Comparing coefficients for Π2​,

    M0L0T0=(L)a2​(ML−3)b2​(L3T−1)c2​

    ∴ a2​=0     b2​=0     c2​=0

    Comparing coefficients for Π3​,

    M0L0T0=(L)a3​(ML−3)b3​(L3T−1)c3​(L)

    ∴ a3​=−1     b3​=0     c3​=0

    Comparing coefficients for Π4​,

    M0L0T0=(L)a4​(ML−3)b4​(L3T−1)c4​

    ∴ a4​=0     b4​=0     c4​=0

    Relationship between Π-groups,

    ρQ2TR2​​=f(QωR2​3​, n, R2​d​, θ)

    #Part (b)

    To ensure dynamic similarity,

    ρQA​2TA​R2,A​​=ρQB​2TB​R2,B​​

    ρQA​2TA​R2,A​​=ρ(1.6QA​)2TB​(2R2,A​)​

    TB​TA​​=1.622​=0.78125

    To ensure dynamic similarity,

    QA​ωA​R2,A​3​=QB​ωB​R2,B​3​

    QA​ωA​R2,A​3​=1.6QA​ωB​(2R2,A​)3​

    ωB​ωA​​=1.623​=5

    To ensure dynamic similarity,

    R2,A​dA​​=R2,B​dB​​

    R2,A​dA​​=2R2,A​dB​​

    dB​dA​​=0.5

    #Question 4

    #Part (a)

    Reynolds number of flow,

    Re=μρVD​

    Re=0.041200(1.2)(0.05)​

    Re=1800

    Since Re<2100, the flow is laminar.

    Friction factor of the pipe,

    f lami​=Re64​=180064​=2258​

    Using the energy equation,

    ρgPA​​+2gVA​2​+zA​=ρgPB​​+2gVB​2​+zB​+hL​

    ρgPA​−PB​​=f lami​⋅Dl​⋅2gV2​

    1200(9.81)PA​−PB​​=2258​(0.0510​)[2(9.81)1.22​]

    PA​−PB​=6144 Pa

    Pressure drop along pipe,

    ΔP=f lami​⋅Dl​⋅2ρV2​

    ΔP=2258​(0.0510​)[21200(1.2)2​]

    ΔP=6144 Pa

    Let total pressure at A be denoted as PA,tot​.

    PA,tot​−ρg(R+x+h)=PB​−ρg(R+x)−ρmano​gh

    PA,tot​−PB​=ρgh−ρmano​gh

    PA,tot​−PB​=(ρ−ρmano​)gh

    Total pressure is the sum of static and dynamic pressure.

    PA,tot​=PA​+21​ρVc​2

    Note that the velocity is the centerline velocity of the flow
    as the manometer probe is placed in the center of the pipe.

    For a laminar flow,

    Vc​=2Vavg​

    Vc​=2(1.2)

    Vc​=2.4 m/s

    Manometer height,

    PA,tot​−PB​=(ρ−ρmano​)gh

    PA​+21​ρVc​2−PB​=(ρ−ρmano​)gh

    6144+21​(1200)(2.4)2=(1200−400)(9.81)h

    h=1.2232 m

    #Part (b)

    If the flow is inviscid, difference in pressures at A and B
    is solely due to dynamic pressure, expressed as 21​ρV2.

    Manometer height,

    PA​−ρg(R+x+h)=PB​−ρg(R+x)−ρmano​gh

    PA​−PB​=ρgh−ρmano​gh

    PA​−PB​=(ρ−ρmano​)gh

    21​ρV2=(ρ−ρmano​)gh

    21​(1200)(1.2)2=(1200−400)(9.81)h

    h=0.11009 m

    #CA1 S2 (2023 - 2024)

    #Question 1

    Water exits a nozzle of 4cm diameter at 4m/s and is directed at an angled plate (blade).
    The fluid has a density of     400 kg/m3. Angle between the two surfaces of the angled
    plate is     60°.

    (a) Determine the force components if the blade is moving towards the nozzle at 1m/s.
    (b) Determine the power of the blade if it is moving away from the nozzle at 1m/s.

    #Part (a)

    Relative velocity of fluid at CV inlet,

    Vin,rel​=4+1=5 m/s

    Using Bernoulli’s equation,

    Vout,rel​=Vin,r​=5 m/s

    Relative mass flow rate,

    m˙rel​=ρAnoz​Vin,rel​

    m˙rel​=400π(0.02)2(5)

    m˙rel​=2.5133 kg/s

    Linear momentum along x-axis,

    ∑Fx​=(m˙V)out​−(m˙V)in​

    Fx​=m˙rel​(−Vout,rel​cos60°−Vin,rel​)

    Fx​=2.5133(−5cos60°−5)

    Fx​=−18.850 N

    Horizontal force acts to the left.

    Linear momentum along y-axis,

    ∑Fy​=(m˙V)out​−(m˙V)in​

    Fy​=m˙rel​(Vout,rel​sin60°−0)

    Fy​=2.5133(5sin60°)

    Fy​=10.883 N

    Vertical force acts upwards.

    #Part (b)

    Relative velocity of fluid at CV inlet,

    Vin,rel​=4−1=3 m/s

    Using Bernoulli’s equation,

    Vout,rel​=Vin,rel​=3 m/s

    Relative mass flow rate,

    m˙rel​=ρAnoz​Vin,rel​

    m˙rel​=400π(0.02)2(3)

    m˙rel​=1.5080 kg/s

    Linear momentum along x-axis,

    ∑Fx​=(m˙V)out​−(m˙V)in​

    Fx​=m˙rel​(−Vout,rel​cos60°−Vin,rel​)

    Fx​=1.5080(−3cos60°−3)

    Fx​=−6.7858 N

    Horizontal force acts to the left.

    Power of the blade,

    P=Fx​V

    P=6.7858(1)

    P=6.7858 W

    Note that only the x-component of the force generates
    power as it acts in the direction of motion of the blade.

    #Question 2

    Water of density 1000 kg/m3 flows through the given horizontal pipe system.
    The total power loss of the pipe system is     W˙tot​=14 kW.

    (a) Determine the gauge pressure at point 3.
    (b) Determine the head loss between points 1 and 3.

    A (m2)Pavg​ (kPa)Vavg​ (m/s)
    10.6202
    20.25?
    30.5?0.7

    #Part (a)

    Fluid velocity at point 2,

    A1​V1​=A2​V2​+A3​V3​

    0.6(2)=0.2V2​+0.5(0.7)

    V2​=4.25 m/s

    Mass flow rate at each point,

    m˙1​=1000(0.6)(2)=1200 kg/s

    m˙2​=1000(0.2)(4.25)=850 kg/s

    m˙3​=1000(0.5)(0.7)=350 kg/s

    Using the energy equation,

    2g(A2​)2Q2​[(A1​A2​​)2−1]=ρgΔP​

    Qideal​=A2​ρ(1−D2​4/D1​4)2ΔP​​

    Note that the volume flow rate derived is

    across the Venturi meter.

    Qf​=0.0025π(8.9821)

    Qf​=0.070545 m3/s

    Average rate of discharge,

    Qavg​=20.074445+0.070545​

    Qavg​=0.074948 m3/s

    Time taken to empty pool,

    t=Qavg​V​

    t=0.07494825(10)(2.5)​

    t=8339.1 s=2.32 hr

    #Part (c)

    • Use a larger diameter pipe — reduces relative roughness and thus f
    • Use an elbow with a larger radius — reduces loss coefficient
    • Use an inlet with a rounded lip — reduces loss coefficient
    • Use pumps arranged in parallel to increase flow rate
